name: Aaron Hill
credit: No confirmed portrait sourced for this archive.
bio: Aaron Hill (1685–1750) was an English dramatist, poet and projector, a patron of younger writers and a correspondent of Pope and Richardson. His verse was collected in his Works (1753).

The poem here is the one printed under his name in Frederick Locker's Lyra Elegantiarum (London: E. Moxon, 1867), an anthology of vers de société and vers d'occasion by deceased authors; the texts follow that first edition.

poems.title: As lamps burn silent with unconscious light
poems.author: Aaron Hill
poems.collection: Lyra Elegantiarum, ed. Frederick Locker (London: E. Moxon, 1867)
poems.text:
As lamps burn silent with unconscious light.
So modest ease in beauty shines most bright,
Unaiming charms with edge resistless fall,
And she who means no mischief does it all.

poems.title: A Strong Hand
poems.author: Aaron Hill
poems.collection: The Home Book of Verse, ed. Burton Egbert Stevenson (1912)
poems.text:
Tender-handed stroke a nettle,
And it stings you for your pains;
Grasp it like a lad of mettle,
And it soft as silk remains:

So it is with these fair creatures,
Use them kindly, they rebel;
But be rough as nutmeg graters,
And the rogues obey you well.
